name: databricks-sdk-py-verified-content-transfers
instr:
The Databricks SDK cannot verify the integrity of logical content it reads, downloads, imports, writes, or uploads. Add opt-in cryptographic verification of the caller-visible byte sequence, independent of chunking, concurrency, retries, fallbacks, or multipart execution. An expected digest or size may be required, with a stable completed result available only after successful delivery or publication.

Every verified HTTP, DBFS, concatenated, Files, and workspace stream must count logical bytes once in delivery order. Mark `integrity_result` complete only after all content is delivered or acknowledged. Closing, seeking, partial consumption, and concatenated-stream boundaries must preserve native cursor, response, child ownership, and close behavior, without presenting stale or incomplete evidence as complete. Seeking concatenated content invalidates obsolete completion evidence without changing established cursor behavior.

Sequential, parallel, resumable, multipart, DBFS, Volumes, and workspace transfers must reconcile only committed bytes. Failed, retried, abandoned, or fallback transports contribute only bytes later delivered or acknowledged. HTTP chunks and parallel ranges may finish physically out of order, but verification follows logical file order. DBFS blocks and multipart parts retain native completion rules while representing one ordered acknowledged source sequence.

Verified downloads are transactional: a mismatch neither replaces an existing destination nor leav
